_README: Query corpus for measuring menu()/route() recall over the jCodeMunch catalog.
LEAKAGE DISCIPLINE (read before adding a query):
Each query MUST be written as the task a user actually has, phrased in the
user's vocabulary, WITHOUT the target tool's name or description in view.
A query built by paraphrasing a tool description measures paraphrase matching,
not retrieval, and will score near-perfectly for the wrong reason. The harness
computes a per-query leakage score (shared rare tokens with the target's
name + description) so this stays measured rather than promised. See
benchmarks/README.md and the planted_queries.json precedent: a max-leakage
corpus is a fixture, never a retrieval score.
TARGETS: 'targets' lists every action that would be an ACCEPTABLE answer.
'ideal' (optional) is the single best action when one clearly dominates.
Recall@k credits any member of 'targets'. Precision@1 credits only 'ideal'
when present. Multi-target entries are deliberate: several questions in this
domain have more than one defensible answer, and a harness that pretends
otherwise measures the author's opinion instead of the router.
TARGET AUDIT 2026-08-02 (v1.108.218). The retrieval counterfactual shipped in
v1.108.217 surfaced that this corpus violated its own rule above: a query lost
to get_repo_map, which is a correct answer its target list omitted. Every one
of the 59 target lists was then re-reviewed against the catalog descriptions
in ALPHABETICAL order, deliberately WITHOUT consulting any ranking -- using
'what currently ranks high' as the candidate generator is the leakage
mechanism itself, because every accepted correction would then raise the score
by construction. Test applied: would a user receiving this action's output
consider the question answered, without needing a different call?
Result: 12 additions across 12 queries, 0 removals. The asymmetry is disclosed
rather than balanced -- manufacturing a removal for symmetry would be a worse
error than the asymmetry. Two over-generous targets were considered and KEPT
because the case against each was arguable, not clear: get_symbol_diff on
'which symbols changed between these two commits' (it diffs snapshots, not
commits) and register_edit on 'I just edited a file, refresh it' (it
invalidates caches without re-indexing).
The five misses this audit deliberately did NOT rescue are the ones where the
proposed action genuinely cannot answer -- e.g. route offers get_blast_radius
for 'what breaks if I change the POST orders endpoint', and get_blast_radius
does not accept an endpoint. Those stay misses.
A recall figure measured after this audit is NOT comparable with one measured
before it. The pre-audit number was route@1 42.4 / @3 59.3, menu@1 40.7 /
@3 61.0; quote the delta as a corpus correction, never as a routing gain.
